fields.h1: Build a Webinar Registration Form That Sends the Join Link
fields.hero_description: Build a webinar registration form that emails each registrant the join link and saves every registration to a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the webinar registration form along with the emails and seat limits that each new registration sets in motion.
fields.feature_1:
The join link arrives with the confirmation

The app emails each registrant a confirmation with the join link, the date, and the start time as soon as they submit. Registrants never wait on a host to send the link by hand.
fields.feature_2:
Reminders on the schedule you set

Set reminders for 24 hours and 1 hour before the start, or any gap you prefer, and each one repeats the join link. A registrant who cancels from the email gets no further reminders.
fields.feature_3:
A seat cap, with a waitlist behind it

Cap each session at the seat count you choose. Once it fills, the form takes waitlist signups instead and offers the next person in line a seat when a registrant cancels.
fields.feature_4:
Qualified registrants land in your CRM

Ask for company size and role, and the app sends registrants who match your rule to the CRM you connect, through its API. Everyone else still gets the join link and reminders.
fields.feature_5:
Every registration is a row you own

Each registration saves as a row in a database you own, tagged with the link that brought the registrant in. Compare the newsletter link with a partner post by seats filled.
fields.feature_6:
Take the code when the defaults stop fitting

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can add a field, a new session format, or a custom report and keep the registrations you already have.

fields.usecase_heading: One Form, Four Kinds of Webinar
fields.tab_content_1:
38 of 214 registrants go straight to sales

Tollbridge Payroll runs a product demo every month and asks each registrant for company size. Of 214 registrants for the October demo, 38 work at companies with 200 or more employees. Those 38 sync to the CRM as sales leads, and account executive Ravi Kulkarni gets an email listing them before the demo starts.
fields.tab_content_2:
Waitlisted registrants move up when a seat opens

Duvall Business Center splits its small business workshop into 3 sessions of 100 seats each. The Cash flow session filled with 12 people on the waitlist. When one registrant canceled, the seat went to Ivo Szalai, first in line, along with a confirmation email and the join link. The other 11 are still waiting.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every registrant sees the start time in their own time zone

Haugen Marine Sensors hosts the same webinar twice on Thursday, Nov 12, at 9:00 AM and 6:00 PM Eastern. The form asks for a time zone along with the session. Joris Vandermeer in Rotterdam picks 9:00 AM, and his confirmation page and both reminders show it as 3:00 PM, his time.
fields.tab_content_4:
Hearthwise opens the session knowing all 61 questions

Hearthwise Energy asks each registrant for its heat pump webinar to pick a topic and type a question. The 61 questions arrive grouped as cost 24, setup 22, and repairs 15. Once attendance syncs from the connected webinar platform, the 143 of 310 registrants who did not join get the replay link.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Webinar Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a webinar registration form that sends the join link and reminders, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the form is for
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the times and the seat cap
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write the emails people will get
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the job the registrations do after the submit. A demo that feeds sales needs company size and role; an internal training session needs a name and a work email. Write down what happens to each registration before you add a single field.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask only for what the session or the follow-up uses. A name and an email cover the join link, and every extra field should change a reminder, a routing rule, or the host's prep. Mark the rest optional, or cut it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Enter the date, each session time with its time zone, and the seat count per session. Then decide what happens at the cap: close the form, or open a waitlist that offers freed seats in the order people joined it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Draft the confirmation first, then choose how far ahead each reminder goes out. Put the join link in every reminder as well as the confirmation, since the last reminder is the email registrants open right before the session starts.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the form in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the decisions from the first four steps into one prompt, written the way you would brief a colleague, and add where qualified registrants should go. Emergent builds the form with its registrations database and email steps, and changes any part when you prompt again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sign up once with your own address before the link goes out. Check that the confirmation arrives with the right join link, that the start time reads correctly in your time zone, and that the registration shows up as a new row.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Give the newsletter and each social post its own version of the registration link. After the webinar, compare seats filled by link, and plan the next session's promotion around the channel that brought in the most registrants.

faq_plan.q: What is a webinar registration form?
faq_plan.a: A webinar registration form is the page people fill out to reserve a place at an online session. It collects at least a name and an email, plus any session time or question the host asks for, and each submission triggers the confirmation that carries the join link.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a webinar registration form?
faq_plan.a: Open Emergent's AI form builder and describe the webinar in plain English: who it is for, when it runs, and what registrants should receive. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, and you change any part by prompting again. Test it with your own email before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a webinar registration form include?
faq_plan.a: Start with a name and an email, which is all the join link needs. Add a session time when you run more than one, a time zone for an international audience, and company size or role only if sales will act on them. A question box gives the host material for the live Q&A.

faq_plan.q: How is a webinar registration form different from an in-person event form?
faq_plan.a: The difference is what happens after the submit. A webinar form must deliver a join link, remind people before a fixed start time, and show that time in each registrant's time zone. An in-person registration form can stop once the details are saved and the venue address is on the confirmation.

faq_plan.q: When should a webinar registration form send reminder emails?
faq_plan.a: Send two: one 24 hours before the start and one an hour before, each with the join link. Schedule them from the start time rather than the signup date, so someone who registers that morning still gets the 1-hour reminder.

faq_plan.q: How does a webinar registration form deliver the join link?
faq_plan.a: Through the confirmation email that goes out as soon as the form is submitted, and again in every reminder. Keep the link off the public registration page so only registrants have it. Emergent builds the app that sends the confirmation and the reminders by email.

faq_plan.q: Can a webinar registration form limit the number of seats?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each session a seat count, and once the last seat goes, new registrants join a waitlist instead of the session. The same cap-and-waitlist logic runs a summer camp registration form, where each week holds a fixed number of spots.

faq_plan.q: Should a webinar registration form close before the session starts?
faq_plan.a: Only if you need a final count first. Leaving it open until the start time works, because a late registrant still gets the confirmation with the join link straight away. Close it early when the host needs the list for breakout groups or a seat cap.

faq_plan.q: Where do webinar registration form responses go?
faq_plan.a: They go to a registrations table, where each submission is a row with the name, email, session, and every answer. With Emergent, that table sits in a database you own, with no response caps, and the app can sync it to a CRM or any other tool with an API.

faq_plan.q: Can one webinar registration form handle several sessions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. List each session with its own time and seat cap, and let registrants pick one or several; every choice saves to the same row. For a multi-day event with tracks, badges, and in-person sessions, a conference registration form is the better fit.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits between webinar platform help pages (registration settings inside one platform's meeting tool) and template galleries from form builders that collect a name and an email. Neither covers the work after someone registers. This page shows a webinar registration form that emails the join link, sends reminders, caps seats with a waitlist, routes qualified registrants to the CRM, shows each start time in the registrant's own time zone, and collects questions ahead of the session, with every registration kept as a row the host owns. The FAQ answers the setup questions a host asks: which fields to ask for, confirmation and reminder timing, seat limits, sharing the registration link and session times.
